name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd
title: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd - 543374 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset manager with flows still below market growth; Q4 equity yield fell 2-3 bps and PAT dropped to ₹187 crore on lower other income, while management claims flows are improving from a low base.

triggers.quote: the overall reduction is a very , very marginal, narrowed quite significantly

triggers.quote: the broad impact generally post the regulatory changes is in the range of about 3 to 4 basis points, roughly

triggers.quote: It used to be somewhere around about 45% to 50% for the industry I'm talking about. It went up to almost about 92% for the industry.

guidance.quote: With the improved flows , broadly I would say , we should come reasonably close to the market growth momentum very soon.
the Board has proposed a dividend of ₹25.5 per share

summary.headline: ABSLAMC Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7% YoY to ₹458 crore, while PAT fell to ₹187 crore from ₹228 crore on lower other income; FY26 PAT ₹975 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was ₹458 crore versus ₹429 crore a year earlier, and operating profit rose to about ₹252 crore from ₹233 crore. Reported PAT fell to ₹187 crore from ₹228 crore, which management attributed to lower other income from mark-to-market actions. For FY26, revenue was ₹1,845 crore (₹1,685 crore), operating profit ₹1,015 crore (₹944 crore) and PAT ₹975 crore (₹931 crore); the Board proposed a dividend of ₹25.5 per share. Average AUM including alternates reached ₹4.74 lakh crore (up 17% YoY), with equity MF AUM up 17% to about ₹1.97 lakh crore. Management said flows and SIP registrations improved QoQ, but market share is still slightly down.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹429 crore in Q4 FY25 (+7% YoY)
vs ₹228 crore in Q4 FY25; lower other income from mark-to-market
Management described it as about 75% of profit distributions
Harshit T's back-calculation implied about 2-3 bps QoQ decline; management cited telescoping and product mix

segments.name: Mutual fund (overall)
segments.commentary: Average AUM including alternates ₹4.74 lakh crore (+17% YoY); MF quarterly average AUM ₹4.36 lakh crore (+14% YoY); equity MF average AUM about ₹1.97 lakh crore (+17% YoY).

segments.name: Passive / ETF
segments.commentary: Quarterly average passive AUM ₹41,200 crore (+25% YoY), crossing ₹40,000 crore; ETF AUM grew 68% YoY vs industry ETF growth of 40%. ETF AUM about ₹11,500 crore including gold and silver; 54 passive products; 16.91 lakh folios.

segments.name: PMS and AIF
segments.commentary: PMS and AIF AUM ₹32,570 crore at Q4 FY26 vs ₹11,300 crore at Q4 FY25 (about 3x), including ESIC mandate of about ₹28,400 crore; ex-ESIC AUM grew 14% YoY. Revenue share about 6% gross and 3.5% net of total revenue.

segments.name: Real estate AIF
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹740 crore, up 51% YoY; fundraising under way for Aditya Birla Real Estate Credit Opportunities Fund Series II.

guidance_outlook: SEBI regulatory change from April 1 (TER/commission structure) expected to impact equity AUM yield by about 3-4 bps broadly; management aims to keep AMC profitability neutral to positive via commission and cost restructuring, rollout in the current quarter, with no exact figure quantified.
EPFO equity mandate agreements signed; operationally ready to receive inflows within days, with fixed income mandate for five years expected to start in the current quarter.
Expect ESOP cost impact of ₹8-10 crore per quarter in FY27; employee cost increase described as marginal.
Plans to add several new locations in FY27 and to launch the APEX SIF offerings in the near term, with GIFT City ABSL Global Emerging Market Fund Series II soon.
Management aims to reach near market growth momentum soon as market share decline narrows.
capex_capacity: Employee count at 1,650 as of March 2026 end; plans to add one or two members for passive business build-out.
New ESOP scheme rolled out in FY26 at about ₹845 price, covering about 110 employees.
Incorporated wholly-owned subsidiary Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC International IFSC Limited at GIFT City and obtained retail license.
Launched APEX SIF vertical with first offering APEX SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund; added two specialists for long-short and derivatives strategies.
Present in about 19,000+ pin codes; plans to add several new locations in FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry quarterly average AUM ₹81.5 lakh crore at March 2026 (+21% YoY); industry record SIP contribution about ₹32,000 crore in March 2026 (+24% YoY).

ABSLAMC SIP contribution ₹1,204 crore in March 2026 (+11% QoQ from ₹1,080 crore); quarterly SIP contribution about ₹3,600 crore; SIP book about ₹76,000 crore (down from about ₹87,000 crore last quarter purely due to MTM).
New SIP registrations about 6.71 lakh in the quarter vs 5.4 lakh in the prior quarter; total investor folios 1.1 crore.
SIP cancellations rose during volatility; industry cancellation ratio reportedly rose to about 92% from 45-50%; ABSLAMC cancellations were lower than the industry.

Active equity flows improving: arbitrage, Flexi Cap, Multi Asset Allocation, Multi-cap, Balanced Advantage, GenNext, small and midcap; about 85% of equity funds delivered Q1 and Q2 performance. Two additional products added to bank recommendation lists (HDFC Bank, Kotak).
Management said last year's flows were twice the prior year's; flows now expected to be well above ₹250-300 crore per month net, though not quantified.
Fixed income flows were pressured in March quarter by bank deposit competition and rate volatility; normalised in April with running number about ₹445 crore (unit not specified in call).

qa_highlights.question: What is the mitigation plan for the 3-5 bps regulatory impact from April 1 and the net impact on AMC books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated the impact at about 3-4 bps and said structures will be redesigned across commissions and other expenses to keep AMC profitability neutral or positive, without quantifying the number.

qa_highlights.question: How have flows and market share moved this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Flows improved QoQ with better acceptance and banking approvals; the market share decline has narrowed significantly and management expects to come close to market growth soon.

qa_highlights.question: Key data points: SIP AUM, ETF AUM, PMS/AIF revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: SIP book about ₹76,000 crore (down QoQ purely on MTM); ETF about ₹11,500 crore of ₹41,200 crore passive AUM; PMS/AIF revenue about 6% of gross revenue and 3.5% net.

qa_highlights.question: Why did equity yield decline about 2-3 bps QoQ and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to telescoping pricing and product mix (including growth in passives), not a specific one-off; versus last year the drop is 2-3 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Expected employee cost growth and ESOP impact?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP impact of ₹8-10 crore per quarter from FY27; headcount at 1,650 with normal attrition of about 50 and onboarding of 80-100 off-role staff; cost increase expected to be marginal.

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹250-300 crore of monthly net equity inflows now a steady base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the trend supports it and the number would be much higher than indicated, though it would not give a figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the banking channel strategy and product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Two products are on HDFC Bank's recommendation list and two or three on Kotak's; banking flows had fallen when products were off lists. Pipeline includes SIF launch soon, lifecycle funds, REIT/InvIT funds pending SEBI approval, and open-ended GIFT City EM fund.

risks_watch: Regulatory TER and commission restructuring from April 1; management has not quantified the net impact and distributor reaction is unknown.
Equity yield down about 2-3 bps QoQ (62-63 bps now); telescoping and mix shift could continue.
Market share still declining, though at a narrower rate; flows must improve to match industry growth.
Rising SIP cancellations during volatility; SIP AUM fell to about ₹76,000 crore on MTM.
Other income is volatile: Q4 PAT fell 18% YoY on mark-to-market, so reported PAT can diverge from operating profit.
Rupee depreciation and FII outflows from geopolitical conflict in West Asia remain near-term risks.
EPFO mandate fund inflows and ESOP cost step-up (₹8-10 crore per quarter) to monitor in Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the flow and performance recovery and the alternates and passive growth, but cautious and non-specific on the regulatory impact, which was not quantified. Some answers on yields, the net flow base and regulatory mitigation were vague or deferred.
key_quotes: we will try and make it neutral to everyone and win -win for the overall business without having any kind of deep impact either for the distribution community or for our AMC business.
I think the broad impact generally post the regulatory changes is in the range of about 3 to 4 basis points, roughly.
our SIP cancellations were actually lower than the industry , I would say.
So, I would say materially different from the past. Our flows had come down quite significantly from this channel, because products were not part of the recommendation list.

adds.what: Several new locations planned in FY27 (no count given; present in about 19,000+ pin codes)
APEX SIF vertical with first offering APEX SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund (product launch, not productive capacity)

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects market share to come reasonably close to industry growth 'very soon' on improving flows, with EPFO mandates and new locations/products in FY27 but none quantified, and a 3-4 bps SEBI TER yield headwind.
